blocks.orig: There are some animals that are truly fascinating. One animal that is pretty high up this list is the giraffe. From a young age, we are taught that giraffes are magnificent creatures. But are giraffes friendly?
blocks.html: Some animals are genuinely captivating, and the giraffe ranks fairly high on that list. We learn early in life that giraffes are majestic animals. But are giraffes friendly?

blocks.orig: Their long necks make them totally unique, and their magnificent size leaves tons of people wanting to see these creatures in person.
blocks.html: Nothing else looks quite like them thanks to their long necks, and their impressive size makes countless people want to see them up close.

blocks.orig: Until you see a giraffe in person, you will not be able to understand just how breathtaking these animals are.
blocks.html: Only when you stand in front of a giraffe will you grasp how breathtaking these animals really are.

blocks.orig: You can probably see giraffes in a zoo near you, but for the best experience, you should see these creatures in their natural habitat.
blocks.html: A zoo near you may well have giraffes, but to get the most out of the experience, you should see them in their natural habitat.

blocks.orig: Giraffes are not one of the big five, but they are a big part of why so many people go on game drives during safaris in Tanzania.
blocks.html: Although giraffes are not part of the big five, they are a major reason why so many people head out on game drives on safaris in Tanzania.

blocks.orig: You might have visions of yourself meeting a giraffe for the first time, and even striking it. But one thing you might want to ask yourself first is “are giraffes friendly?”.
blocks.html: Perhaps you imagine meeting a giraffe for the first time and maybe even stroking it. Before you do, though, it is worth asking yourself “are giraffes friendly?”.

blocks.orig: It is easy to assume that these magnificent beasts will be gentle and friendly, but that isn’t necessarily the case. In this guide, we’ll have a look at whether, or not, giraffes are friendly.
blocks.html: You might easily assume that these majestic animals are gentle and friendly, but that is not always true. This guide looks at whether giraffes are friendly or not.

blocks.orig: Most people know what giraffes are, but just in case, let’s have a look. Well, as we have said, giraffes are magnificent creatures that are most famous because of their unique experience.
blocks.html: Most of us know what a giraffe is, but let’s take a quick look just in case. As mentioned, giraffes are majestic animals best known for their unique experience.

blocks.orig: Giraffes have incredibly long necks that allow them to eat leaves directly from trees.
blocks.html: Their remarkably long necks let giraffes eat leaves straight from the trees.

blocks.orig: It is these long necks that make these animals so famous because there really are no other creatures quite like them on the planet.
blocks.html: These long necks are what make the animals so well known, as there is truly nothing else quite like them on Earth.

blocks.orig: Giraffes hail from Africa. They have a coat pattern that is made up of irregular splodges that is instantly recognizable.
blocks.html: Giraffes come from Africa. Their coat has a pattern of irregular blotches that you recognise at once.

blocks.orig: There are actually 4 different species of giraffe, but all 4 have a fairly similar appearance. To put it bluntly, you will always be able to recognize a giraffe, it is not a species that will confuse you.
blocks.html: In fact, there are 4 different species of giraffe, yet all 4 look fairly alike. Put simply, a giraffe is always easy to identify; it is not a species you will mix up with anything else.

blocks.orig: By 4 years of age, giraffes will reach their adult height. They normally measure between 4.5 and 5.5 meters, depending on whether they are male (a bull) or female (a cow).
blocks.html: Giraffes reach their full adult height by 4 years of age. Depending on whether they are male (a bull) or female (a cow), they usually stand between 4.5 and 5.5 meters tall.

blocks.orig: They will continue to gain weight as they age. Giraffes will typically live for up to 25 years in the wild, and there are an estimated 68,000 giraffes living in the wild, with around 28,850 of these giraffes living in Tanzania.
blocks.html: As they grow older they keep putting on weight. In the wild, giraffes usually live for up to 25 years; an estimated 68,000 giraffes live in the wild, and around 28,850 of them are found in Tanzania.

blocks.orig: While they are not considered endangered, giraffes are a “vulnerable” species as their natural habitat is being lost, and they are at risk of illegal hunting. But are they friendly? Let’s find out.
blocks.html: Giraffes are not classed as endangered, but they are a “vulnerable” species because they are losing their natural habitat and face the risk of illegal hunting. So are they friendly? Let’s see.

blocks.orig: Generally speaking, yes, giraffes are friendly. These creatures tend to have gentle personalities and aren’t a species that would actively attack a human being.
blocks.html: On the whole, yes, giraffes are friendly. They usually have a gentle nature and are not a species that would go out of its way to attack a person.

blocks.orig: So, even though these creatures are massive, you don’t need to worry about them attacking you if you encounter one in the wild. Unless they feel threatened, giraffes are unlikely to lash out.
blocks.html: So despite their enormous size, there is no need to fear an attack if you come across one in the wild. Giraffes are unlikely to strike out unless they feel threatened.

blocks.orig: There are a number of creatures in the wild that aren’t particularly friendly, or at least won’t act in a friendly manner when you first encounter them.
blocks.html: Plenty of wild animals are not especially friendly, or at least will not behave in a friendly way when you first meet them.

blocks.orig: Most of these animals are animals which hunt prey. Giraffes are herbivores, so they do not hunt their food. Instead, they simply feast on shoots and leaves from the acacia tree.
blocks.html: Most of those are predators that hunt prey. Giraffes, as herbivores, do not hunt for their food. They simply feed on the shoots and leaves of the acacia tree instead.

blocks.orig: Giraffes are grazers, so they do not have the aggressive tendencies associated with hunting to survive.
blocks.html: Because giraffes are grazers, they lack the aggressive streak that comes with hunting to stay alive.

blocks.orig: Giraffes are pack animals, so when you see them in the wild, they will often move around in large groups. They live like this to protect themselves from the threat of other animals.
blocks.html: Giraffes live in herds, so in the wild you will often see them moving about in large groups. This way of life helps protect them against other animals.

blocks.orig: There are lots of predators in the wild that will hunt giraffes if other food sources aren’t available.
blocks.html: Many predators in the wild will go after giraffes when there is no other food around.

blocks.orig: While giraffes do not tend to be aggressive against these predators, they do travel in groups to ensure that they are safe, and not vulnerable.
blocks.html: Giraffes are not usually aggressive towards these predators, but they move in groups so they stay safe rather than exposed.

blocks.orig: Many predators will attack giraffes while they are drinking from the watering hole, as their bent over position gives access to the neck.
blocks.html: A lot of predators strike when giraffes are drinking at the watering hole, because bending over leaves the neck exposed.

blocks.orig: By travelling in a pack, half of the giraffes can drink while the other half keep watch for predators.
blocks.html: Moving as a group means half of the giraffes can drink while the rest look out for predators.

blocks.orig: However, giraffes rarely drink from a watering hole. As part of their aversion to aggression, giraffes tend to get the majority of their hydration through the leaves and shoots that they feast upon.
blocks.html: That said, giraffes seldom drink at a watering hole. In keeping with their dislike of conflict, they get most of their moisture from the leaves and shoots they eat.

blocks.orig: Generally, giraffes are peaceful and friendly creatures. But do they like humans? Let’s find out.
blocks.html: On the whole, giraffes are calm and friendly animals. But do they like people? Let’s see.

blocks.orig: Before we answer this question, it is important to differentiate between wild giraffes, and giraffes in captivity.
blocks.html: Before answering, it helps to distinguish between giraffes in the wild and giraffes kept in captivity.

blocks.orig: Giraffes in the wild are very different because they will not have a lot of interaction with humans, whereas giraffes in captivity will regularly see humans throughout their day-to-day life.
blocks.html: Wild giraffes are quite different, as they have little contact with people, while giraffes in captivity see people all the time in their everyday lives.

blocks.orig: While giraffes are friendly creatures, this friendliness doesn’t mean that you should approach them.
blocks.html: Giraffes may be friendly animals, but that does not mean you should go up to them.

blocks.orig: As we have said, giraffes will rarely attack unless they feel threatened, but this doesn’t mean that you should simply walk up to them and force yourself upon them when you see them in the wild.
blocks.html: As mentioned, giraffes seldom attack unless they feel threatened, yet that is no reason to stroll up to them and impose yourself on them when you spot them in the wild.

blocks.orig: These animals may be mild-mannered, but they are also wild animals. They are not domesticated, and they are not used to interacting with humans.
blocks.html: They may be gentle by nature, but these are still wild animals. They are not tame, and they are not accustomed to dealing with people.

blocks.orig: While this friendliness may differ from giraffe to giraffe, generally giraffes in the wild will not like humans.
blocks.html: How friendly they are can vary from one giraffe to the next, but in general wild giraffes do not like people.

blocks.orig: However, this differs for giraffes raised in captivity. There are a lot of giraffes raised in captivity across the world, and mostly these giraffes will be more friendly to humans than wild giraffes.
blocks.html: It is a different story for giraffes raised in captivity. Many giraffes around the world grow up in captivity, and these are usually friendlier towards people than wild giraffes.

blocks.orig: Giraffes in captivity are dependent on humans, and they have a lot more interaction with humans. Especially giraffes that are born and raised in captivity.
blocks.html: Captive giraffes rely on people and have far more contact with them, particularly giraffes that are born and raised in captivity.

blocks.orig: Even then, giraffes in captivity are usually only friendly to their keepers. So, you shouldn’t approach a giraffe in captivity unless there is a zookeeper present.
blocks.html: Even so, captive giraffes are normally friendly only towards their keepers. You should therefore not go near a giraffe in captivity unless a zookeeper is with you.

blocks.orig: While these animals aren’t aggressive, their large size could put you at risk if they get spooked. So while these creatures are friendly, it is still best to watch giraffes from a distance.
blocks.html: These animals are not aggressive, but their sheer size could put you in danger if something startles them. So although they are friendly, it is still wisest to watch giraffes from a distance.

blocks.orig: In short, yes, giraffes are friendly creatures. However, this doesn’t mean that you should approach them in the wild.
blocks.html: So, in short, yes, giraffes are friendly animals. Even so, you should not approach them in the wild.

blocks.orig: If a giraffe feels threatened, it will lash out to protect itself and its offspring. So it is best to simply observe these magnificent creatures from a distance.
blocks.html: When a giraffe feels threatened, it will strike out to defend itself and its young. The best approach is simply to watch these majestic animals from a distance.
